name: Check Every Triple
summary: Sort the array, then test every combination of three indices i < j < k and keep the ones whose values sum to zero (skipping duplicates).
visualizationIntent: init: sort the array and show an empty result list. outer-loop: anchor i on the first value of the triple. middle-loop: place j after i. inner-loop: sweep k after j as the moving cursor. check: highlight nums[i], nums[j], nums[k] and show their sum; when the sum is zero flash the three cells green and, if the triple is new, add it to the result. return: freeze on the collected unique triples.

lineExplanations.3: Sort the array so equal values sit together, which makes duplicate triples easy to skip.
lineExplanations.4: Store the length so the three loops know where to stop.
lineExplanations.5: Create an empty result list that will collect every zero-sum triple.
lineExplanations.6: Anchor the first index i of the triple.
lineExplanations.7: Choose the second index j strictly after i.
lineExplanations.8: Sweep the third index k strictly after j.
lineExplanations.9: Add the three selected values to test this triple.
lineExplanations.10: Check whether the three values sum to exactly zero.
lineExplanations.11: Build the concrete triple from the three chosen values.
lineExplanations.12: Only keep this triple if it is not already in the result, avoiding duplicates.
lineExplanations.14: Return every unique zero-sum triple found.

syntaxExplanations.1: class Solution: defines the class wrapper expected by the platform.
syntaxExplanations.2: def threeSum(self, nums): defines a method that receives the array nums.
syntaxExplanations.3: nums.sort() reorders nums in place from smallest to largest.
syntaxExplanations.4: n = len(nums) stores how many numbers are in the array.
syntaxExplanations.5: result = [] creates an empty Python list for the answer triples.
syntaxExplanations.6: for i in range(n): loops i over every index of nums.
syntaxExplanations.7: for j in range(i + 1, n): loops j over every index after i.
syntaxExplanations.8: for k in range(j + 1, n): loops k over every index after j.
syntaxExplanations.9: total = nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] adds the three selected values.
syntaxExplanations.10: if total == 0: runs the block only when the three values cancel out.
syntaxExplanations.11: triple = [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] builds the three-number list.
syntaxExplanations.12: if triple not in result: is true only when this exact triple was not stored before.
syntaxExplanations.13: result.append(triple) adds the new triple to the answer list.
syntaxExplanations.14: return result sends back all unique zero-sum triples.
